title: Single field return, dead short VDD-to-GND, 48 V industrial gateway line card

samples.condition_as_received: de-soldered from customer board by the customer's CM; package intact, no external discoloration visible at 10x; pin 7 (VDD) solder residue present
samples.disposition: consumed - decapped and cross-sectioned; mount retained in case file

samples.condition_as_received: known-good unit, same date code, pulled from customer spares
samples.disposition: returned to customer, non-destructive imaging only

chain_of_custody.action: unit removed from installed gateway, bagged
shipped with RMA form; board not included
received, photographed as-received before any handling
2D X-ray, unit returned to bag same day
GATE D1 cleared and signed; wet chemical decap of SN-0416
GATE D2 cleared and signed; FIB cross-section at the localized site

complaint: Unit went dead in the field after approximately 400 hours of service. Customer reports the gateway is hot-swapped into a live 48 V backplane during maintenance. Customer's own bench check found VDD shorted to GND. Customer states 'this is ESD from our handling' and has asked us to confirm.

symptoms.failure_rate: 1 unit; no other returns from this customer or this date code to date. Installed base on this platform approximately 12,000 units.
symptoms.conditions: Failure discovered in service. Customer bench check: VDD-GND resistance measured at approximately 3 ohms with a DMM. No other pin checked.

problem.what: One returned KL-8842-QFN32 exhibits a low-resistance short between VDD (pin 7) and GND; measured 2.8 ohms on the curve tracer at 100 mV, symmetric in both polarities.
problem.is_not: Not present on any signal pin: all 28 I/O pins curve-trace within the known-good envelope. Not a package crack (X-ray and C-SAM clean). Not present in any other returned unit - zero further returns from date code 2548.
problem.where: Customer A industrial gateway platform, field-installed units subject to hot-swap maintenance into a live 48 V backplane.
problem.when: After approximately 400 service hours; discovered during a maintenance visit.
problem.how_many: 1 of approximately 12,000 units in the installed base on this platform (0.008%); 1 of 1 units received for analysis.
problem.since: First and only report; RMA received 2026-08-05.

d0_emergency_response: No line stop. Date code 2548 was placed on ship-hold for 48 hours while the returns database was queried for related signatures; hold released once no second occurrence was found.

team.name: DE-05
team.role: Product design - ESD/EOS protection network owner

team.name: AE-01
team.role: Applications engineering - customer board and sequencing

observations.conditions: 10x and 50x stereo, as received, before any electrical test
observations.result: Faint mold discoloration over the die corner nearest pin 7 at 50x oblique; no cracking, no bulging, no rework marks.
observations.interpretation: Consistent with localized internal heating. Not diagnostic alone.

observations.conditions: Pin-by-pin I-V, +/-1 V sweep, compliance limited to 1 mA to avoid altering the damage
observations.result: VDD (pin 7) to GND: 2.8 ohms, linear and symmetric in both polarities. All 28 I/O pins and their protection diodes match the reference unit envelope. No leakage on any signal pin.
observations.interpretation: Observed: a resistive, non-rectifying short on the supply path only. A metallic (fused/melted) path, not a degraded junction.

observations.conditions: Final-test datalog retrieved by serial from the 2548 date code archive
observations.result: Unit passed all final-test parameters at manufacture with normal margin, including IDDQ and all I/O leakage tests.
observations.interpretation: Retires the escape-at-final-test hypothesis for a pre-existing defect of this magnitude.

observations.result: All 32 bond wires intact and correctly placed; no wire sweep, no shorting, no foreign metal, die-attach void area visually below the 10% device limit.
observations.interpretation: Retires wire-short and gross-assembly hypotheses. Null result, reported.

observations.conditions: Immersion C-SAM, die face and die-attach interfaces; performed before any decap or bake
observations.result: No delamination detected at the die face, die attach, or leadframe interfaces. No popcorn crack.
observations.interpretation: Null result. Retires the moisture/popcorn chain; run before decap because decap would have destroyed the evidence either way.

observations.conditions: 50 mA forced through the VDD-GND short, 3 Hz modulation, through-mold
observations.result: A single hot spot located over the die corner adjacent to the pin-7 bond, coincident with the external mold discoloration.
observations.interpretation: Failure site localized to a sub-millimetre region without opening the package. This localization is what cleared GATE D2 later.

observations.conditions: GATE D1 cleared 2026-08-12: all N0-N2 complete, C-SAM and X-ray done, single-sample protocol acknowledged, expected outcomes pre-registered, customer approval on file. Wet acid decap, window over the pin-7 corner.
observations.interpretation: Enabling step; no diagnostic content of its own.

observations.conditions: 100x-500x, before any re-biasing of the die
observations.result: A molten region approximately 60 x 40 micrometres spanning the VDD bus metal and the adjacent supply clamp, with visibly displaced and re-solidified metal and cracked dielectric at the perimeter. The pad-side I/O protection structures are undamaged and identical to the reference die.
observations.interpretation: Observed: a large-area melt on the supply path. The scale and metal displacement are far beyond what a human-body-model event can supply, and the I/O ESD network is intact.

observations.conditions: GATE D2 cleared 2026-08-15: site localized by thermography and optical, all prior imagery archived, expected outcomes pre-registered. FIB cut through the centre of the melt.
observations.result: Metal fully fused through the full metal-1 thickness over approximately 12 micrometres, with re-solidified metal bridging into the substrate through a cracked ILD.
observations.interpretation: Observed: a metal-to-substrate fused path - the physical short measured on the curve tracer.

observations.conditions: SEM at the cut face; EDX at the melt and at a clean reference site 200 um away
observations.result: Al and Si intermixed within the melt; no Cl, Br, or S above the reference site; no foreign material.
observations.interpretation: Retires corrosion and contamination hypotheses. Consistent with a purely thermal/electrical event.

hypotheses.hypothesis: ESD (HBM) during customer handling - the customer's stated cause
hypotheses.evidence_for: Customer handles boards during maintenance; no ESD control audit exists for the field procedure.
hypotheses.evidence_against: Damage is on the supply path, not on a pin protection device; all 28 I/O protection structures are undamaged; the melt volume (~60x40 um with displaced metal) exceeds the energy a human-body event can deliver through ~1.5 kohm.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: curve_trace pin map plus internal_optical damage-area measurement

hypotheses.evidence_for: CDM damage can appear on internal nodes rather than at pads.
hypotheses.evidence_against: CDM damage is sub-micron with minimal surrounding melt; the observed site is three orders of magnitude larger in area and shows metal displacement. Unit also passed 400 service hours after assembly.

hypotheses.hypothesis: EOS - sustained supply-sourced overstress on VDD during live hot-swap
hypotheses.evidence_for: Melt confined to the VDD bus and supply clamp; metal fused over ~12 um; mold discoloration above the site; energy required is only available from a supply, not from a stored-charge model; application is hot-swapped into a live 48 V backplane.
hypotheses.evidence_against: The customer has not supplied the schematic or inrush measurements, so the specific transient path is inferred, not measured.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Application inrush measurement on the customer's board during hot-swap - requested, outstanding.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Latch-up triggered by the hot-swap transient, sustained by the 3.3 V rail
hypotheses.evidence_for: Latch-up produces supply-sourced melt indistinguishable from EOS by morphology, and a hot-swap transient is a plausible trigger.
hypotheses.evidence_against: The melt path runs through supply bus metal rather than through a well-substrate diffusion path; no evidence of the parasitic structure conducting was found in cross-section.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Board-level transient capture plus a latch-up characterization on fresh units per JESD78-style method - recommended, not yet run.

hypotheses.evidence_against: The short was measured by the customer before receipt, and our first curve trace ran at 1 mA compliance. Damage predates our handling.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: As-received custody log and the customer's own bench measurement

mechanism.primary: Electrically induced physical damage (EIPD) on the VDD supply path, most consistent with a sustained electrical overstress (EOS) event rather than a component-level ESD event.
mechanism.basis: Observed: 2.8 ohm symmetric VDD-GND short (curve trace); a ~60x40 um melt with displaced metal spanning the VDD bus and supply clamp (internal optical); metal fused through full metal-1 thickness with a re-solidified path into the substrate through cracked ILD (FIB cross-section); no elemental contamination (EDX). All 28 I/O protection structures undamaged, which is inconsistent with a pin-level ESD event. The damaged volume requires more energy than component-level ESD models can supply, and is consistent with a supply-sourced transient. Confidence is medium rather than high because the application transient has not been measured and latch-up has not been positively excluded.
mechanism.secondary: Latch-up triggered by the same transient cannot be excluded on morphology alone; the cross-section did not show a well-substrate conduction path, which argues against it but does not eliminate it.
mechanism.not_determined: The specific circuit path and magnitude of the hot-swap transient. The customer has not supplied the board schematic or inrush measurements, so the source of the overstress is inferred from the damage and the stated application, not measured.

escape_point: Two legs. (a) Manufacturing test cannot detect this failure because the part was good at manufacture - the final-test datalog for SN-0416 shows normal margin on every parameter including IDDQ and I/O leakage, so there is no test escape. (b) The real escape is at the application-review stage: the datasheet absolute-maximum and the recommended hot-swap sequencing were never reviewed against this customer's live-backplane maintenance procedure, and no inrush limiting is specified in our reference design for hot-swap use.

containment.action: 48-hour ship-hold on date code 2548 pending a returns-database query for matching signatures (VDD-GND short).
containment.verification: Returns database query across 18 months: zero further VDD-GND shorts on this part number.

containment.action: Advisory to the customer: do not hot-swap this line card into a live backplane until inrush behaviour on the 3.3 V rail has been characterized.
containment.verification: Advisory acknowledged in writing by Customer A quality on 2026-08-07.

containment.action: Retain and quarantine any further returns from this platform unpowered, without customer bench testing, to preserve the damage signature.
containment.verification: RMA desk instruction updated; distributor confirmed.

corrective_actions.action: Applications engineering to characterize hot-swap inrush on the customer's board and publish a hot-swap application note with required inrush limiting and rail sequencing for this device family.
corrective_actions.verification: Measured inrush waveform on the customer board, before and after the recommended limiting, attached to the application note.

corrective_actions.action: Design review of the supply-clamp energy rating against the transient environment implied by live-backplane hot-swap; decide whether the clamp is adequately specified or the datasheet must state the limit explicitly.
corrective_actions.verification: Design review record with the clamp energy calculation and the resulting datasheet or design change decision.

corrective_actions.action: Run a latch-up characterization on fresh units per a JESD78-style method to positively include or exclude the latch-up leg of the mechanism.
corrective_actions.verification: Characterization report; result folded back into this case's mechanism call before the case is treated as fully closed.

validation: Returns-database query across 18 months and approximately 12,000 installed units found zero further VDD-GND short signatures - the failure is a single event, not a population trend. (Evidence: query export dated 2026-08-06 in the case file.)
Customer acknowledged the hot-swap advisory in writing on 2026-08-07; no further returns from this platform as of case closure.

PENDING: effectiveness of the corrective actions cannot be validated until the application note and the latch-up characterization are complete. This report records the actions as open, not as verified.
prevention: Read-across: identify every other product family sold into hot-swap or live-insertion applications and check whether the datasheet states a hot-swap limitation. Owner DE-05.
Process change: add 'live insertion / hot-swap present?' as a mandatory field in the application-review checklist for new design-ins. Owner AE-01.

FA process: add the standing instruction that returned units are quarantined unpowered and are not bench-tested by the customer or the distributor before receipt, so that damage evidence is not altered en route. Owner QE-02.
recommendations: Obtain the customer's board schematic and an inrush capture during hot-swap; without it the transient source remains inferred.
Complete the latch-up characterization before treating the mechanism call as final.
If a second unit with the same signature is ever received, run magnetic current imaging before opening it - a second sample is worth more intact than decapped.
limitations: Single sample. Every conclusion is a 'consistent with' at the unit level and none of it supports a population claim.

The customer measured the short with a DMM before shipping the unit; that measurement applied power to an already-damaged part and could in principle have extended the damage. The morphology does not suggest it did, but it cannot be excluded.
The application transient was not measured. The source of the overstress is inferred from the damage character and the stated hot-swap usage.
Latch-up was not positively excluded; the cross-section evidence argues against it but is not conclusive.
No sibling units from date code 2548 were available for comparison.
